brief: North Macedonia's listed-bank disclosure landscape is unusually well-centralised: essentially every price-sensitive filing from Komercijalna, NLB, Stopanska, Halkbank, Sparkasse, UNI Banka, TTK and peers flows through SEI-Net (seinet.com.mk), the Macedonian Stock Exchange's statutory electronic disclosure system, which the exchange re-broadcasts as a dated, issuer-tagged RSS feed at mse.mk/mk/rss/seinet — a near-ideal ingestion spine confirmed live in this pass with a bank filing dated 21.8.2026. The MSE layers per-issuer profile pages (/mk/issuer/{slug}, with audited/unaudited statements, quarterly income statements and prospectus PDFs in a predictable /Repository/ object store) plus listing rules and corporate-governance compliance reports on top of that stream. The regulator KHV (sec.gov.mk) is the complementary, structurally separate node: it approves prospectuses and share/bond emissions, keeps participant registers including authorised and depository banks, and records its actual decisions in narrative Месечни извештаи rather than a filterable bank register — so capital-raise detection is a parsing job, not a feed subscription. Main technical caveat: SEI-Net document pages appear client-side rendered and yielded empty bodies to plain fetch (a rendering limitation, not evidence the source is dead), so production collection should assume headless rendering or a discovered JSON endpoint.
